description: links (ADR 0031, ADR 0015): what a concept body's footnotes make of the map, said once for both tiers. The api derives a concept's LINKS_TO edges at every governed write (`packages/core/src/store/map/index.ts`) and the worker derives them again in the full rebuild (`apps/worker/src/better_answers_worker/links.py`); an edge's id carries its link's ordinal, so the two must count links alike or the rebuilt map and the live one name different edges. A footnote reference `[^label]` is a **citation mark** when its label, trimmed, with inner whitespace collapsed and compared without case, is the `id` of an entry in the concept's `sources` list. A mark resolves to the first entry carrying that id, whether or not the body holds a definition for it, and it is never a link: it makes no edge and takes no ordinal. A footnote reference whose label is no source id is a link when the body defines it, and it then takes an ordinal and makes an edge when its definition names a concept, as OKF allows. One with neither a source nor a definition is plain text: no edge, no ordinal, no error. A footnote definition line `[^label]: ...` is never a link and takes no ordinal. Everything else in the prose that today takes an ordinal still does. Only a record-form `sources` entry carries an `id`; a string-form entry carries none, so no mark resolves to it. Every case is read as the concept `citing` below, every target is a concept IRI no concept holds yet (so both tiers make the edge with no kind and no lookup), and no source's resource is a concept, so no case makes a lineage edge. `links` is every LINKS_TO edge the case makes, in ordinal order, by ordinal, target, `section` and `sentence`. `section` is the text of the nearest heading above the link, or null, and `sentence` is the sentence the link sits in, with each link reduced to its text. Both are trimmed, with each run of whitespace made one space. `marks` is every citation mark, as written, with the index of the `sources` entry it resolves to, in body order. Throughout, a line ends at a line feed alone, whitespace is the six characters space, tab, line feed, carriage return, form feed and vertical tab, a line holding only whitespace is blank and ends a paragraph, and a scheme is an ASCII letter followed by ASCII letters, digits, plus, full stop and hyphen. The TypeScript half drives the api's map write (`packages/core/test/links.contract.test.ts`) and the Python half the worker's edge derivation (`apps/worker/tests/test_links_contract.py`).

cases.case: a source-id mark is no link and shifts no ordinal
cases.body:
Claims close within 30 days.[^a] See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) for tiers.

[^a]: https://better-answers.com/c/01J6PPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPP

links.sentence: Claims close within 30 days.^a See the product for tiers.

cases.why: The mark names a source, so even a definition that is a concept IRI makes no edge, and the ordinary link after it is the body's first link.

cases.case: a footnote defined as a concept IRI and naming no source is a link
cases.why: OKF allows a footnote to link a concept; `b` is no source's id, so the footnote stays a link and takes the first ordinal.

cases.case: a mark with no source and no definition is plain text
cases.body: Receipts are kept for six years.[^c] See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN).

links.sentence: Receipts are kept for six years.^c See the product.

cases.why: `c` names no source and the body defines nothing for it, so it is text: no edge, no ordinal, no error.

cases.case: a repeated source id resolves to its first entry
cases.why: Two entries share `a`; the mark resolves to the first of them, never the second.

cases.case: a source-id mark with no definition still resolves
cases.body: Expenses over 500 pounds need a director's approval.[^a]
cases.why: A mark resolves through the `sources` list, not through a footnote definition, so a body that defines nothing for it still cites the source.

cases.why: A string-form entry names a resource and no id, so a mark spelling that resource resolves to nothing and is plain text.

cases.why: An image, an external link and a label the body never defines each still take an ordinal and make no edge; only the citation mark and the footnote definitions take none. A full reference's label and a definition's are compared ignoring case and spacing. A footnote's definition is found the same way, however its label is spaced or cased.

cases.case: quoted code holds no link and no mark
cases.body:
A span `[^a]` and a longer one ``[quoted](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN)`` hold nothing, and `one` and `[two](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN)` hold nothing either.

```md
[fenced](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) and [^a]
```

Only [this one](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6PPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPPP) maps.[^a]
cases.why: Code spans and fenced blocks are text, so neither a link nor a mark inside one counts, however many spans of one length a line holds, and the one link outside them takes the first ordinal.

cases.case: a caret in an inline link or a reference is no mark
cases.why: Only a bare footnote reference can be a citation mark. An inline link whose text starts with a caret, and a full reference whose label does, are links like any other, even where the label names a source.

cases.case: a blank source id names no mark

links.sentence: Claims close within 30 days.^ See the product.

cases.why: An id that is only whitespace is no id, so an empty footnote label resolves to nothing and is plain text.

cases.case: a fence opens only at the start of a line
cases.body:
Mileage is paid ~~~ at cost, see [the rates](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN).
~~~

links.sentence: Mileage is paid ~~~ at cost, see the rates.

cases.why: A run of tildes or backticks opens a fenced block only where a line starts with it, so a run mid-line leaves the link after it in the prose.

cases.case: adjacent marks are two marks, not a reference

[^a]: The staff handbook.

links.sentence: Approvals need two signatures.^a See the product.

cases.why: Two marks written side by side cite two sources. Neither is the label of a reference link, so neither takes an ordinal.

cases.case: only plain whitespace is trimmed from a label
cases.body: Claims close within 30 days.[^﻿a] Mileage is paid at cost.[^a] See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN).

links.sentence: Claims close within 30 days.^﻿a Mileage is paid at cost.^a See the product.

cases.why: Space, tab, line feed, carriage return, form feed and vertical tab are the whitespace a label loses. A byte-order mark or a next-line character is part of the label, so neither label here names the source.

cases.case: a definition starts only after a line feed
cases.body:
Mileage follows the rates policy.[^b][^b]: https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN

Rates are reviewed yearly.[^c] [^c]: https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
cases.why: A carriage return alone or a line separator does not start a line, so neither definition here defines anything, and both footnotes are plain text.

cases.case: a bracket run is one link naming nothing
cases.why: A run of brackets before the first `]` is one bare link of the whole span: it names nothing and takes the first ordinal, and the readable link after it takes the next. However many brackets a body holds, the reader walks it once.

cases.case: an unclosed fence blanks the rest of the body
cases.why: A fence that no line closes runs to the body's end, and every link inside it is blanked with it, so nothing inside maps. The reader costs one walk, wherever the fence ends.

cases.case: a definition's target may sit on a later line
cases.why: The definition's target is the first run after the colon that is more than the six, and the six include line feeds, so the target may sit on a later line. The definition line itself is a link naming nothing and takes the first ordinal; the reference resolves to the target and takes the next.

cases.case: a space is whitespace in a label and around a definition's target
cases.why: A space is one of the six, so the reference's label reads as `the rates` and the definition's target is the run between the space after the colon and the next one. The reference resolves to the concept and takes the first ordinal; the definition line names nothing.

cases.case: a tab is whitespace in a label and around a definition's target
cases.why: A tab is one of the six, so the reference's label reads as `the rates` and the definition's target is the run between the tab after the colon and the next one. The reference resolves to the concept and takes the first ordinal; the definition line names nothing.

cases.case: a heading line ends only at a line feed
cases.body:
# Claims andexpenses 

See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN) for tiers.
All of them.
cases.why: An edge carries the heading above its link and the sentence the link sits in. A line ends at a line feed alone, so a carriage return or a line separator inside a heading is part of its line. Only the six whitespace characters are trimmed and made one space, in a heading and in a sentence, so the carriage return becomes a space and the line separator stays where it is written.

cases.case: only plain whitespace marks a heading or ends a sentence
cases.body:
# Expenses
#﻿Draft

Claims close.﻿See [the product](https://better-answers.com/c/01J6NNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN)or <https://example.test/a﻿b> and <https://example.test/cd>. Next one.

links.sentence: Claims close.﻿See the productor https://example.test/a﻿b and https://example.test/cd. Next one.

cases.why: A heading's marks need one of the six whitespace characters after them, so the line after a byte-order mark is no heading and the one above it stands, with its next-line characters kept. A sentence ends at a full stop that one of the six or the paragraph's end follows, so a full stop before a byte-order mark or a next-line character ends nothing. Neither character stops an autolink, so both autolinks lose their angle brackets.

cases.case: a heading's code span leaves one space
cases.why: A heading is read from the prose, where a code span is blanked to spaces, and its whitespace runs become one space. So the heading reads the same however each tier counts the characters of an emoji it blanked.

cases.case: an autolink's scheme is ASCII alone
cases.why: A scheme is an ASCII letter, then ASCII letters, digits, plus, full stop and hyphen. The Kelvin sign and the long s fold to k and s under Python's case-insensitive matching, but neither is in the scheme, so neither bracketed run is an autolink, takes an ordinal or loses its angle brackets.

cases.case: a line of whitespace is a blank line
cases.why: A line ends at a line feed alone, so in a CRLF body the line between two paragraphs holds a carriage return. A line holding only the other five whitespace characters is blank, and a blank line ends a paragraph, so a link's sentence never runs into the heading or the paragraph above it.
